newsitem.title: MONACO: TENNIS-SANTORO TOPPLES ANOTHER CLAY SPECIALIST.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SANTORO TOPPLES ANOTHER CLAY SPECIALIST.

text.p: Frenchman Fabrice Santoro notched his second consecutive upset at the Monte Carlo tennis Open on Thursday, toppling Spain's Sergi Bruguera two days after beating Austrian Thomas Muster.

With his 3-6 7-5 6-1 victory over the tournament's 16th seed, Santoro has defeated two of the best clay court players in the world, both former French Open champions who between them have also won five titles here.
"I had not won many matches coming here so these two victories are very important to me," said the 24-year-old Frenchman, currently ranked a modest 90th in the world.
"I rank them among the three or four best wins of my career."
Another Spanish favourite, Albert Costa, bid an early farewell to the tournament. Costa, losing finalist in the principality last year, was beaten by Chile's Marcelo Rios 7-6 6-4.
The losses, the latest in a long list of upsets in the tournament, left Wimbledon champion Richard Krajicek as the big favourite to win the title.

The tall Dutchman easily won his clash of big servers against Australian Mark Philippoussis 6-3 6-2. After losing the first three games, during which Philippoussis hit three serves at over 215 kph, Krajicek cruised through the rest of the match, winning in just over an hour.
"At first, when I saw him serve, there was nothing I could do. You only hope it's not going to last," said the fourth-seeded Dutchman.
"But I feel better every day and I've recovered from the jet lag I had from flying from Japan," said Krajicek, a winner in Tokyo last week.
He now faces a real test against Spain's Carlos Moya, seeded sixth, who beat Ukraine's Andrei Medvedev 6-4 7-6.
But it was the way Santoro beat Bruguera, as much as the result itself, which dominated conversation around the courts.

The short Frenchman used to be a typical clay court player, making up for his lack of power by a lot of running behind the baseline. Yet against a lacklustre Bruguera, he rushed to the net 61 times, producing fine volleys like a player bred on grass.
"This year I realised I could not go on as I did before if I wanted to make a career. I was a ball fiddler. My game belonged to the 1970s more than to the 1990s," he said.
"I realised I did not have enough power to score from the baseline so I decided to try my luck at the net."
In the quarter-finals, Santoro will meet Spanish qualifier Carlos Costa, who dismissed another Frenchman, Arnaud Boetsch, in straight sets 6-4 7-5.
Rios, who avenged his defeat to Albert Costa in the semifinal last year with his win, will meet Sweden's Magnus Larsson, conqueror of American world number one Pete Sampras in the previous round.
Larsson eased past Czech Daniel Vacek 7-5 6-0.

Spaniard Alex Corretja survived a tense battle against Czech Bohdan Ulihrach. The 12th seed, winner in Estoril two weeks ago, won 4-6 7-6 6-0. His quarterfinal opponent will be Norway's Christian Ruud.
